analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 11.6.26
key_insights: Futures bid on 11/6 (Nasdaq +130bps, S&P +10bps, Russell +10bps) after a tech-led sell-off on 11/5: Nasdaq -6.4%, SOX -12%, AI-data-center-levered basket -12%, Momentum Long -11%.

Desk flows on 11/5 showed steady supply across semis and data-center-levered names with very limited defense. SOXL, SOXX, SMH, QQQ and TQQQ traded record or near-record volume, and the desk calls it the highest put-volume day ever.

Heavy inbound inquiries about fund and investor stress across the system. GS PB says TMT funds fell more than 4% and are now roughly flat YTD, after about +24% on average before the June/July AI sell-off. Multi-strats fell 1.4% on average.
Nasdaq's VIX (VXN) had its largest 1-day change since Covid.

Bounce drivers cited: oversold conditions (SOX 14-day RSI of 26, only two lower readings in the last decade), a $25bn LRCX buyback (stock +11% pre-market), constructive European tech action (ASML +7%), and benign comments from the Texas governor-elect on data centers.
GS European trading notes its desk has moved to 1 standard deviation to Buy, versus 2 standard deviations to Sell the day before.

SPX had its worst day since April 2025 and NDX its worst day since March 2020. VVIX had its largest 1-day move since February 2018, and 11/5 was the largest put-volume day in CBOE history (over 11mm puts).

NET beat: revenue 6% above the Street and accelerated about 3.5pp to 39% y/y, the fastest growth in about 4 years. 4Q revenue guided to +37.5% y/y, 6% above the Street. Stock +21% pre-market, driven partly by agentic traffic and faster renewals.

TEAM fell about 16-17% pre-market. F1Q Cloud revenue grew +31% y/y against a +28.5% guide, but F2Q Cloud revenue is guided to about +27% y/y, a deceleration, against elevated expectations. FY guidance was raised.

ABNB beat and raised: Q3 gross bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat GSe and the Street. FY26 revenue growth guide raised to high-teens % y/y from mid-teens. Stock +12% pre-market. Negatives were cancellation rates at 19% (vs 16% a year ago) and take rates modestly below expectations.

MCHP F2Q results were in line, but F3Q guidance is below the Street: revenue about $1.61bn vs Street $1.63bn, non-GAAP gross margin 64.5% vs Street 66.5%, EPS $0.91 vs Street $0.95. Stock -1% pre-market.

Reuters reports Silver Lake and PIF held talks to acquire Unity at about $25bn before its latest earnings. Unity's market cap is now about $21.5bn and shares rose about 4% after hours. No deal is certain.
Elon Musk said Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for more Cybercab production.

GIR published a note on risks to its US data center capacity forecasts after several gubernatorial flips from Republican to Democratic and campaigns for stricter data center regulation in Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Georgia and Michigan.
Overnight reports say Qatar's Emir spoke to Trump about de-escalating the Iran war. NFP is due this morning, with GS at +75k vs +65k consensus.

GS PB: global fundamental L/S managers fell 1.3% (a -2 SD move), mostly from market/beta exposure, and are +8.7% YTD. Systematic L/S managers rose 0.2% and are +16% YTD. Multi-strats fell 1.4%, with Momentum down 3.7 SD.

Research: GS reiterates Buy on LYFT with the price target cut to $20 from $22, reiterates Buy on LYV after a 3Q26 beat, keeps Neutral on YELP with the PT cut to $23 from $24, and is cautious on OPEN after weak unit economics.

earnings_insights: ABNB Q3'26 (reported): gross bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat GSe and Street estimates. FY26 outlook raised to revenue growth in the high-teens % y/y (from mid-teens) and adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 36% (from at least 35.5%). Q4'26 adjusted EBITDA margin guided down slightly y/y. Cancellation rate 19% vs 16% a year ago.
NET Q3'26 (reported): revenue 6% above the Street, up 39% y/y, EPS 11% above (FactSet). Q4 revenue guide of +37.5% y/y is 6% above the Street and EPS guide is 13% above (FactSet).

TEAM F1Q (reported): Cloud revenue +31% y/y vs guide of +28.5%, subscription ARR +23% y/y, non-GAAP operating margin 32% vs guide of 28.5%, about $464mn FCF. F2Q Cloud revenue guided to about +27% y/y with non-GAAP operating margin about 26%. FY Cloud revenue guide raised to 26% from 25.5%.

MCHP F2Q (reported): revenue $1.62bn vs GS $1.62bn and Street $1.61bn, EPS $0.97 vs GS $0.96 and Street $0.94, gross margin 66.5%. F3Q guide (company guidance vs estimates): revenue $1.61bn at midpoint vs GS $1.65bn and Street $1.63bn, non-GAAP EPS $0.91 vs GS $0.98 and Street $0.95. $53mn of unusual F2Q revenue contributions inflates the comparison.

LYV 3Q26 (reported): revenue $10.11B vs consensus $9.60B, AOI $1.18B vs $1.15B, attendance 61.1M vs 56.7M, fee-bearing tickets 98.3M vs 91.5M. FY26 attendance now expected to approach 180M and Ticketing AOI growth to be high-single-digit %.
LYFT Q3'26 (reported): adjusted EBITDA ahead of GSe and Street. North America rides growth accelerated for a second quarter and management expects further acceleration in Q4.
YELP Q3'26 (reported): Other revenue +82% y/y, core advertising revenue down y/y. Management targets a $250m annualized run rate for Other revenue exiting 2028.

OPEN 3Q26 (reported): 2,728 homes sold, 4,865 purchased. Contribution margin 3.3% vs GSe 5.1% and consensus 3.7%. Adjusted EBITDA loss of $31mn vs a $4mn loss in 2Q26. Aged inventory over 120 days rose to 18% from 9%. 4Q26 guide: revenue growth of at least 40% y/y and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $70-85mn.
